chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْه، عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَطِيَّةَ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn 'Atiyya who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ لِعَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ بْنِ أَعْيَنَ: كَيْفَ سَمَيْتَ ابْنَكَ ضُرَيْسًا؟ فَقَالَ: كَيْفَ سَمَاكَ أَبُوكَ جَعْفَرًا؟ قَالَ: إِنَّ جَعْفَرًا نَهْرٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَضُرَيْسُ اسْمُ شَيْطَانٍ

translations.en: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan: How did you name your son Dhurays? He said: How did your father name you Ja'far? He said: Ja'far is a river in Paradise, and Dhurays is a name of a devil.

en.summary: In this narration from Al-Kashi’s *Ikhtiyar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) engages Abd al-Malik ibn A'yan to contrast the celestial virtue of 'Ja'far' (a river in Paradise) with the inferential association of 'Dhurays' with a devil, illustrating the Shia emphasis on the spiritual weight of names. This dialogue underscores the tradition of selecting names that invoke divine blessings or reflect positive attributes, a practice deeply rooted in the Imams' teachings on personal identity and spiritual destiny.
en.seo_question: What is the meaning and significance of the name Dhurays according to Imam al-Sadiq?

key_terms.ضُرَيْس: Dhurays, a name of a devil
